answer: The grove test I would run is Verified milliner society membership with millinery association attestation: a membership the association kept across years of hats, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a membership the association kept across years of hats — so privacy survives, and the mesa is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the inlet of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
